name: Browser Preferences
location: Firefox: prefs.js (profile root) ; Chrome/Edge: Preferences (JSON, profile root)
purpose: Configuration data associated with the browser application, including privacy settings and synchronization preferences.
key_fields: Firefox: sync status, last sync time, artifacts selected to sync
normal_baseline: Sync tied to a single known account; privacy and clear-on-exit settings consistent with organizational policy or the user's established habits.
anomalies: Sync account_info referencing a personal or unauthorized account on a corporate device, indicating possible data exfiltration via browser sync
clear_data_on_exit or an equivalent privacy setting enabled shortly before or during an incident window, suggesting deliberate anti-forensic staging
site_engagement/media_engagement scores showing heavy interaction with a domain otherwise absent or sparse in History
parsing_tools: Manual JSON review (text editor / JSON viewer)
anti_forensic_notes: Preferences/prefs.js is a live file rewritten frequently during normal use, so it reflects only the current/recent configuration; prior settings changes are not versioned unless captured through other means (backups, Volume Shadow Copies).
interpretation: Firefox's prefs.js exposes sync status, last sync time, and which artifact categories (history, passwords, bookmarks, etc.) are configured to sync. Useful for tracing data that may have propagated to another device. Chrome's per_host_zoom_levels, media_engagement, and site_engagement values are indirect but useful proxies for how much a user actually interacted with a given site, beyond a simple visit count. Edge preferences additionally carry account_info and clear_data_on_exit/sync settings.
